words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) carries the prior question into the recitation scene instead of starting a detached report. Because it is the first segment of {{ar:وَإِذَا}} ({{tr:wa-idhā}}), the boundary link and the time-condition arrive together: the earlier diagnosis is now shown through what happens whenever the Qur'an is recited to them.

topics.headline: diagnostic link into the recitation test
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah does not open a detached topic; it carries the prior reproach into a concrete test scene.
topics.reason: QAC marks {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) as the opening conjunction segment, and attachment evidence links the following condition to the negated response, so the CRITICAL claim that the connector resumes the prior diagnosis is locally supported.

topics.headline: bound connector fused to the temporal frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that boundary-link and time-condition arrive together in the compact opening {{ar:وَإِذَا}} ({{tr:wa-idhā}}).
topics.reason: The surface segment is immediately followed by {{ar:إِذَا}} ({{tr:idhā}}), and the clause evidence treats the pair as the opening of the recitation condition.

words.prose: {{ar:إِذَا}} ({{tr:idhā}}) makes the ayah a condition-response scene: when the Qur'an has been recited over them, the answer is {{ar:لَا يَسْجُدُونَ}} ({{tr:lā yasjudūna}}). With the perfect passive {{ar:قُرِئَ}} ({{tr:quriʾa}}), the recitation is a completed threshold that recurs, and the absence of a separating answer-particle keeps trigger and refusal tightly adjacent.

topics.headline: recitation condition with direct negated answer
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that recitation is the condition under which the refusal is measured, not merely background information.
topics.reason: QAC identifies {{ar:إِذَا}} ({{tr:idhā}}) as a temporal adverbial particle, and attachment evidence makes {{ar:لَا يَسْجُدُونَ}} ({{tr:lā yasjudūna}}) the response clause.

topics.headline: completed recitation as recurring threshold
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the force of whenever: each completed recitation reopens the same test of response.
topics.reason: The temporal particle is followed by the perfect passive {{ar:قُرِئَ}} ({{tr:quriʾa}}), so the CRITICAL threshold reading is supported by local form and clause sequence.

topics.headline: temporal particle inside the fused opener
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the condition is also the prior question's test case because {{ar:إِذَا}} ({{tr:idhā}}) is entered through {{ar:وَإِذَا}} ({{tr:wa-idhā}}).
topics.reason: The word is the second visible segment of the fused opening, and the syntax links that opening to the recitation protasis and negated apodosis.

words.prose: {{ar:قُرِئَ}} ({{tr:quriʾa}}) is passive, so the reciter recedes and the hearers face the recited Qur'an itself; contrastive q-r-ʾ forms leave this local Form I passive intact, with no trainer or named performer taking center stage. Its perfect form under {{ar:إِذَا}} ({{tr:idhā}}) treats each recitation as a completed exposure before the refusal appears, while {{ar:عَلَيْهِمُ}} ({{tr:ʿalayhim}}) makes the event public and directed over them. The q-r-ʾ echo with {{ar:ٱلْقُرْءَانُ}} ({{tr:al-qurʾānu}}) makes the recitation self-identifying; the 7:204 response frame heightens the contrast because recitation there calls for listening and silence, while here it becomes evidence of withheld prostration.

topics.headline: passive recitation suppresses the reciter
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that accountability is framed around the recited message reaching the audience, not around the personality of a named reciter.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify {{ar:قُرِئَ}} ({{tr:quriʾa}}) as passive, with an unexpressed agent and {{ar:ٱلْقُرْءَانُ}} ({{tr:al-qurʾānu}}) as passive subject, matching the CRITICAL deagentivization claim.

topics.headline: perfect aspect makes exposure complete before refusal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the refusal comes after the recitation has fully arrived, not while the exposure is still incomplete.
topics.reason: The form is perfect passive under {{ar:إِذَا}} ({{tr:idhā}}), so the rows that read the event as completed exposure are locally licensed.

topics.headline: recitation delivered over the audience
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verb is not private reading; the following {{ar:عَلَيْهِمُ}} ({{tr:ʿalayhim}}) makes it delivered recitation over hearers.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence forces {{ar:عَلَيْهِمُ}} ({{tr:ʿalayhim}}) as the prepositional complement of the passive verb, narrowing reading toward public recitation delivered to an audience.

topics.headline: q-r-ʾ gathering pressure and act-object echo
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verb and noun share the q-r-ʾ field, making the recited discourse self-identifying before the withheld bodily answer appears.
topics.reason: V4 includes gathering and recitation branches for q-r-ʾ, while local grammar selects recitation; the gathering image survives only as pressure on assembled discourse, not as a replacement sense.

topics.headline: form choice and qiraat sound pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that alternative q-r-ʾ possibilities and hamza easing clarify what remains fixed: passive recitation reaches them, without a trainer or named performer taking center stage.
topics.reason: The derivational family and the qiraat {{ar:قُرِيَ}} ({{tr:quriya}}) are useful as contrast, but QAC preserves the local passive Form I frame, so the topic is kept with scope narrowed to form and sound pressure.

topics.headline: 7:204 response frame contrasts this refusal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same recitation-frame can demand listening and silence (7:204), while here it exposes non-prostration.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows give concrete references, and nothing in local grammar blocks using 7:204 as a response-frame contrast rather than as control over the parse.

topics.headline: recitation turns diagnosis into exhibit
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the prior nonbelief diagnosis becomes observable when recitation occurs and the expected bodily response fails.
topics.reason: The passive recitation clause is the protasis of the conditional scene, and the following negated prostration is its response; the boundary rows are therefore locally coherent.

words.prose: {{ar:عَلَيْهِمُ}} ({{tr:ʿalayhim}}) keeps the diagnosed plural group from 84:20 in view and places them under the recitation. The preposition makes them recipients rather than actors, but its upon-relation also gives the scene pressure: the Qur'an is delivered over them as address and exposure. Because the phrase stands before {{ar:ٱلْقُرْءَانُ}} ({{tr:al-qurʾānu}}), the audience is spotlighted before the recited subject is named.

topics.headline: suffix carries the diagnosed group forward
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the recitation falls on the same group questioned in 84:20, not on a new or generic audience.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies the pronoun as continuing the immediately preceding plural group, supporting the CRITICAL continuity claim.

topics.headline: oblique recipient rather than reciting actor
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the group is positioned as affected recipients of recitation, while the passive verb keeps them from being the reciting agent.
topics.reason: The prepositional phrase is governed by the passive verb as a complement, and the passive agent remains unexpressed.

topics.headline: recitation falls upon the audience
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that recitation is not neutral information transfer; the upon-relation gives the delivery pressure and burden.
topics.reason: The local preposition is {{ar:عَلَى}} ({{tr:ʿalā}}), and attachment evidence governs the pronoun through that preposition, so delivery and exposure remain live without replacing the basic recipient relation.

topics.headline: audience phrase before the named Qur'an
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the audience is placed under recitation before the Qur'an is named, making exposure the structural middle of the clause.
topics.reason: The local order places {{ar:عَلَيْهِمُ}} ({{tr:ʿalayhim}}) between {{ar:قُرِئَ}} ({{tr:quriʾa}}) and {{ar:ٱلْقُرْءَانُ}} ({{tr:al-qurʾānu}}), exactly matching the word-order rows.

words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْقُرْءَانُ}} ({{tr:al-qurʾānu}}) is the explicit nominative passive subject, so the clause centers the recited message rather than the hidden reciter. Its definiteness makes the refusal meet the recognized Qur'an, and its q-r-ʾ noun force holds recitation and revealed corpus together as a performed text. The hamza-lightened reading {{ar:ٱلْقُرَانُ}} ({{tr:al-qurānu}}) changes recitational texture, not the word's authority or role. After the audience phrase, the delayed noun becomes the hinge before {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}), and parallels with 7:204 and 75:18 make this sequel of non-prostration stand out against expected listening or following.

topics.headline: named Qur'an becomes the clause center
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the recited message is explicitly named as the passive subject, so the scene cannot remain vague recitation.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify {{ar:ٱلْقُرْءَانُ}} ({{tr:al-qurʾānu}}) as a definite nominative noun and the passive subject of {{ar:قُرِئَ}} ({{tr:quriʾa}}).

topics.headline: definite known recited discourse
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the refusal meets the recognized Qur'an, not an unidentified speech-event.
topics.reason: The noun is definite, and contextual evidence shows the q-r-ʾ noun field is common and recognitional, supporting the CRITICAL known-text reading.

topics.headline: recitation noun names act and corpus together
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the word names the revealed corpus as recited discourse, so the refused object is a performed text rather than inert doctrine.
topics.reason: V4 supports recitation and Qur'an naming within q-r-ʾ, while the local noun and passive frame select the revealed recited discourse; wider q-r-ʾ branches remain background only.

topics.headline: hamza easing changes sound, not authority
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a recitational sound pressure point: hamza easing affects texture while the definite passive subject remains the same authoritative Qur'an.
topics.reason: The qiraat {{ar:ٱلْقُرَانُ}} ({{tr:al-qurānu}}) can be used as phonetic contrast, but it does not replace the local referent or grammatical role.

topics.headline: recited Qur'an contrasts expected following
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the named recited Qur'an stands where other response frames point toward listening, silence, or following (7:204; 75:18), but here the sequel is non-prostration.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows provide concrete parallels, and local syntax allows them as response-frame contrasts without letting them override the local parse.

topics.headline: delayed subject pivots into negation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the processing movement: the audience is exposed first, the Qur'an is then named, and the clause immediately turns toward negated response.
topics.reason: The word order places the noun after {{ar:عَلَيْهِمُ}} ({{tr:ʿalayhim}}), and the same-root echo with {{ar:قُرِئَ}} ({{tr:quriʾa}}) is locally visible.

words.prose: {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) places the failure exactly on the response verb. It does not undo the recitation event and it is not a command telling anyone not to prostrate; before the indicative {{ar:يَسْجُدُونَ}} ({{tr:yasjudūna}}), it reports an ongoing non-response. Because it opens the apodosis, the answer to completed recitation begins with grammatical absence.

topics.headline: negation lands on the response verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the recitation is not negated; the failure is located precisely in the expected prostrating response.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence links {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) directly to {{ar:يَسْجُدُونَ}} ({{tr:yasjudūna}}), and QAC marks it as negative particle before an indicative imperfect, not a prohibitive command.

topics.headline: negation opens the final response beat
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the answer-slot after recitation begins with absence, so the verse lands on a grammatically marked non-performance.
topics.reason: The clause {{ar:لَا يَسْجُدُونَ}} ({{tr:lā yasjudūna}}) is the apodosis of the {{ar:إِذَا}} ({{tr:idhā}}) frame, so the CRITICAL response-slot reading is syntactically forced.

words.gloss_range: they prostrate or submit by bodily lowering; here negated as continuing non-performance
words.root_gloss_range: s-j-d includes prostrating, humble submission, posture/place nouns, and remote branches; local context selects embodied prostration as the visible sign of submission

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: negative particle scoping over the final verb

words.prose: {{ar:يَسْجُدُونَ}} ({{tr:yasjudūna}}) is the final lexical word, and it arrives under {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}), so closure lands on an act withheld. The verb is active Form I, indicative, plural, and objectless: the issue is the group's own continuing non-performance of the basic prostrating act, not a prohibition, a caused or requested act, an intensified or self-staged posture, or a target-specified phrase. The s-j-d field gives the refusal bodily weight, because the expected lowering before authority is denied when the Qur'an is recited. With the sajda cue after the verse, and echoes of prostration and nearness in 96:19 plus positive prostration in 7:206, the reported refusal becomes a live test for the hearer while the sequence moves from nonbelief in 84:20 to explicit denial in 84:22.

topics.headline: objectless Form I keeps the refused act plain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the withheld act is prostration itself, not a causative, requested, intensified, or target-specified posture.
topics.reason: Attachment and valency evidence identify the verb as intransitive with no object or prepositional complement, and QAC identifies it as active Form I.

topics.headline: indicative plural reports standing group behavior
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verse reports the group's continuing behavior, not a prohibition or a single missed prostration.
topics.reason: The retained plural indicative ending and 3mp agreement are locally identified by QAC and attachment evidence, so the command-reading is blocked and the collective response-pattern survives.

topics.headline: bodily lowering makes nonbelief visible
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that nonbelief takes bodily form: the expected lowering before authority is withheld when the Qur'an is recited.
topics.reason: V4 supports prostration and humble submission for s-j-d, while local recitation context and the sajda cue select embodied prostration as the visible sign; mosque or place-noun branches remain background field, not local sense.

topics.headline: final verb lands as action withheld
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah's last lexical word is not simply an action named, but an action heard under negation as the closure landing.
topics.reason: The final verb is governed by {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) in the apodosis, so closure falls on negated prostration.

topics.headline: sajda marker intensifies the reported refusal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the live irony: the verse reports non-prostration at the point where recitation itself prompts prostration.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows identify the sajda marker as a recitation cue; local grammar does not encode the marker inside the word, so the topic is kept as a performative-textual payoff rather than a morphology claim.

topics.headline: prostration echoes frame the refusal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the withheld prostration reverses prostration-and-nearness language (96:19), echoes positive prostration fields such as 7:206, and carries 84:20's negated-imperfect nonbelief into bodily refusal.
topics.reason: The cited echoes are concrete and compatible with the local parse, so they can function as contrast and boundary linkage without controlling the local grammar.

topics.headline: withheld posture leads into explicit denial
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the adjacent ayah sequence moves from inner nonbelief (84:20), to unperformed prostration (84:21), to explicit unbelief and denial (84:22).
topics.reason: The suffix and implicit subject evidence keep the same plural group in view, and the concrete boundary references in the CRITICAL rows support the sequence-level payoff.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Gathered speech calls for gathered bodily submission.** `ق ر ء:B001` has two accepted variants under one packet ID: collecting and gathering, and gathering speech into recitation. `س ج د:B001` supplies lowering in humble submission. The passive recitation “upon them” gives speech a directed relation to bodies; I infer that gathered utterance calls the hearers into a correspondingly integrated response. Their refusal is a failure to let collected speech reorganize posture.

2. **Recitation as an appointed cycle.** `ق ر ء:B002` likewise preserves two variants: reading/teaching recitation and an appointed time or cycle. Coming after twilight, night, full moon, and successive stages, the cyclical variant becomes newly audible. The packet supplies recitation within a sequence of recurring phases; I infer that each reading is an appointed opportunity for response. “When it is recited” therefore marks a recurring threshold, not information delivered once.

3. **Refusal to lower under a true weight.** `س ج د:B004` supplies bowing, lowering the head, and inclining under weight. Sky and earth accepted their Lord's due in 84:2 and 84:5, while humans now remain unlowered under recitation. The packet supplies cosmic compliance and human posture; I infer that revelation exerts a claim analogous to the command heard by creation. Non-prostration reads as structural resistance to due weight.

4. **The absent embodied mark.** `س ج د:B003` supplies the limbs and mark of prostration, while `ك د ح:B002` and the books establish that human action leaves recordable marks. The packet supplies bodily trace and written trace; I infer that prostration would inscribe assent in action. Their refusal is thus not silent neutrality but the absence of the fitting mark in a surah about records.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Active falsification in 84:22 revealed why no bodily mark of submission appears, while divine knowledge of stored contents in 84:23 showed that nonresponse is not empty. The final believers' intentional work in 84:25 supplied the positive counterpart: recitation can become embodied action rather than remaining heard speech.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Gathered speech calls for an integrated bodily answer.** **Lexical evidence:** `ق ر ء` B001 has two packet variants: variant 2 is gathering speech into recitation, while variant 1 is collecting dispersed things into a whole. The fixed ayah repeats the root in passive verb and proper noun. `س ج د` B001 is humbled prostration, and B003 names the several bodily members and mark of prostration. **Structural cue and role:** the recited collection is placed “upon them,” but their bodies do not collect into the coordinated lowered posture. **Abductive move:** I infer a form-to-response correspondence between verbal integration and bodily integration; the packet does not explicitly state that recitation should assemble the limbs. **Reading change:** `لا يسجدون` becomes failure to let the gathered utterance reorganize the whole body.

2. **A due response-point inside the sequence of stages.** **Lexical evidence:** `ق ر ء` B002’s second variant is an appointed time or cycle, while its first variant is reading and recitation; `ط ب ق` B004 in 84:19 is stage after stage. **Structural cue and role:** the fixed `إذا` presents each occurrence of recitation as a response condition within the ongoing sequence. **Abductive move:** I infer that the cycle variant makes recitation a recurrent due moment at which the next bodily state should occur. **Reading change:** the refusal is not static unbelief only; it is repeated interruption of the proper stage-response cycle.

3. **A posture lexically present in the identity that refuses it.** **Lexical evidence:** fixed `س ج د` B001 is lowered submission; the following `ك ف ر` inventory includes B014, bowed or lowered submission called `تكفير`, even though 84:22 names those who `كفروا`. **Structural cue and role:** explicit non-prostration is immediately followed by a root that contains a dormant submission branch. **Abductive move:** I infer deliberate lexical irony at root level, not equivalence between the two forms. **Reading change:** their refusal reads as suppression of a posture that their own next root can name, sharpening disbelief as embodied withholding.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 84:22 confirms the root-level irony through `ك ف ر` B014’s dormant bowed-submission branch, while its actual verbs enact covering and denial. 84:23 then locates the failed bodily response inside an inward containment process, and 84:25 shows the positive alternative in which assent exits the interior as intentional action.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, üzerinde betimler bulunan ve görüldüklerinde önlerinde eğilinilen belirli sikkeleri ortak biçimde tanıklar. Ancak eğilmenin doğrudan betime mi yoksa betimde gösterilen hükümdara mı yöneldiği kaynak anlatımlarında farklı kurulabildiğinden dal kimliği bu hedef ayrımı belirtilerek kabul edilebilir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal yalnızca betimli ve önünde eğilme davranışıyla tanımlanan sikke adlandırmasına bağlıdır; genel sikke, vergi parası veya her betimli nesne bu kapsama girmez.

lexicalization_scope.note: Mekanik kapsam yalnızca söz öbeğidir; tanım bu özel sikke adlandırmasına bağlı kalır ve bunu çıplak kökün genel para anlamı gibi sunmaz.

facets.statement: Söz öbeği, üzerinde hükümdar veya başka bir varlık betimi bulunan belirli sikkeleri adlandırır.
Bu sikkeler görüldüğünde insanlar üzerlerindeki betimle bağlantılı olarak eğilme davranışı gösterir.
Eğilmenin hedefi kimi anlatımda betimin kendisi, kimi anlatımda ise betimde gösterilen hükümdardır.
